images.title: Highest score or total?
images.purpose: Compare the two batters' four matches as bars, so the one big score and the two totals can be seen together.
images.composition: Two small groups of four vertical bars side by side on one shared baseline, with each group's total in a box underneath and white space between the groups.
exact_structure: One grey (#6B7280) baseline shared by both groups; bar heights to scale, 1 unit per run.

Left group labelled Shubman: exactly 4 teal (#0072B2) bars for matches 1 to 4 with heights 0, 17, 21 and 90; the 0 bar is drawn as a flat line on the baseline; the 90 bar is filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) instead of teal to mark the highest score.
Right group labelled Yashasvi: exactly 4 amber (#E69F00) bars with heights 67, 55, 18 and 35.
Each bar's value written just above it: 0, 17, 21, 90 and 67, 55, 18, 35.
Under the left group a grey (#6B7280) outlined box reading Total 128; under the right group a green (#009E73) outlined box reading Total 175.
Arithmetic check for the reviewer only, NOT drawn in the frame: 0 + 17 + 21 + 90 = 128 and 67 + 55 + 18 + 35 = 175.
rejection: more or fewer than 4 bars in a group
bar heights not in proportion, for example 67 drawn shorter than 55
the purple highlight on any bar other than 90
images.takeaway: One big score shows one match; with the same number of matches the totals compare the whole series.
images.description: Two groups of four bars: Shubman 0, 17, 21, 90 with the 90 bar in purple and Total 128; Yashasvi 67, 55, 18, 35 with Total 175.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Let students first notice the tall purple bar, then compare the totals, then the gap between each player's tallest and shortest bar.

image_decisions.why: Bars show at once that the highest score and the total tell different stories.
